TED Paths Course Syllabus Education for personal renewal and social transformation.

A leading future-ready teacher education university responsive to national and global development goals and directions.

Philippine Normal University is committed to lead innovative, responsive and sustainable teacher education programs that set the standards of future-ready teachers and education leaders.

As the National Center for Teacher Education, the Philippine Normal University commits to provide inclusive, innovative, impactful, and sustainable teacher education programs that produce future-ready teachers and education leaders imbued with the values of truth, excellence, and service. Furthermore, PNU shall ensure the continual improvement of its Quality Management System through compliance with International Quality Standards and statutory and regulatory requirements. PNU shall achieve these commitments through its core functions of instruction, research, extension and production.
The College of Teacher Development (CTD) is committed to the development of innovative teachers and educational leaders through the pursuit of its Goals which are aligned with the Philippine Normal University Vision, Mission, Goals, Strategic Development Plan (SDP) and Quality Objectives.
1. Provide the best teacher preparation and development training through quality, innovative and relevant curricular and co-curricular teacher education programs which will nurture teachers and professionals who are: excellent in their discipline, globally competitive, deeply rooted in one's heritage, empowered and committed to social transformation. (SDP1: Shared Vision of Excellence and SDP 2: Quality Assurance)
2. Advance knowledge generation through quality research in education that are relevant and responsive to the needs of teacher education and promotive of sustainable strategic actions for Nation building and Sustainable Development (SDP1: Shared Vision of Excellence and SDP 2: Quality Assurance)
3. Ensure that the Teacher Education programs are quality assured and its management system is compliant with the highest quality standards both national and global. (SDP 2: Quality Assurance: SDP 9: Sustainability)
4. Promote a culture of sharing through extension collaboration activities, partnership with communities and organizations, sharing of scholarship and expertise to educational institutions, stakeholders and relevant agencies for resource generation, advocacy, sustainable actions and continual improvement. (SDP 8: Responsiveness to Stakeholders; SDP 6: Collaboration and Partnership)

5. Expand strategic network of collaboration and partnership that strategically positions the College of Teacher Development as a leader in relevant scholarly and advocacy initiatives (SDP 6: Collaboration and Partnership)
6. Develop products and programs, both conventional and digital that are relevant to the needs of instruction, supportive of students’ optimal learning, contributory to the needs of the profession and helpful in addressing issues and problems of education. (SDP 7: Product and Service development)
7. Design programs, products and services that promote the PNU brand and CTD as a respected community of scholars providing insights on education and societal issues and concerns. (SDP 4: Branding)
8. Expand international presence in the field of teacher education and relevant fields through effective networking, collaboration, and partnership at the international level. (SDP 5: Internationalization)
9. Support professional development and career advancement of the faculty and staff and the College of Teacher Development through promotion of continual work environment improvement, organizational effectiveness, relevant professional development programs and enhanced faculty-employee-management engagement. (SDP 10: Human Capital Management)
10.Establish well defined systems-based solutions and sustainability practices to ensure efficiency and effectiveness of implementation of CTD programs and procedures. (SDP 3: Systems Based Solutions, SDP Sustainability 9)
11.These goals are envisioned to be achieved through the promotion of CTDs Core function of a) quality instruction, b) relevant research in education and scholarship of teaching, c) culture of sharing through relevant extension and community partnership programs and d) production and publication of relevant instructional materials and other resources.
3TED-SS
The Contemporary World
None
This course explores the interrelationship of globalization, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and sustainability issues, focusing on their impact in the Philippine context. Students will examine economic, political, technological, environmental, and socio-cultural dimensions of globalization, assess SDG progress, and analyze sustainability challenges. Methodology includes lectures, interactive discussions, group projects, and utilization of multimedia resources. Further, students will also learn to use data science and mapping tools to better understand and visualize the complexities of globalization, evaluate SDG initiatives, and analyze sustainability data. By the end of the course, students will critically assess globalization's impact, propose actionable sustainability solutions, and foster informed global citizenship rooted in the Philippine context.

Agents of Systemic Change who are described as individuals, organizations, or entities that work to transform structures, processes, and norms within systems, aiming to create sustainable and positive social, economic, environmental, or political impacts. These agents focus on addressing root causes rather than symptoms, challenging and altering policies, power dynamics, and cultural beliefs to achieve equitable and lasting change
Digitally literate agents of change ● Students actively engage with digital learning environments and critically evaluate information across various platforms. They demonstrate proficiency in using digital tools and technologies for learning and problem-solving.
Transformative agents of change ● Students actively participate in cross-cultural exchanges and advocate for inclusive, equitable, and sustainable practices. They appreciate cultural diversity and engage in actions that promote global understanding and sustainability.

Evidence of Performance

Performance Standard
Having a satisfactory rating/grade or passing performance level set by the course professor using the rubric on each given evidence of performance

Grading System

Based on BOR Resolution No. U-3007 dated June 24, 2019, the following is the grading system of the University:

Grade in Percent 98-100 95-97.99 92-94.99 89-91-99 86-88.99 83-85.99

Course Requirements
Consultation Period Prepared

A student may have a grade consultation a week prior to Week 12 or the Final’s week. No Grade Solicitation is allowed once the final grade is already encoded. A student who wished to clarify his/her final grade must write a justification of his/her request and personally communicate with the course professor. No sending of messages via FB, What’sApp or Viber is allowed. An incomplete grade can be given to a student who failed to submit and comply with the FINAL REQUIREMENT(S). The student is expected to communicate with the course professor and file completion form, submit and comply with the requirement immediately after the beginning of the next term. The extension of submission of requirement is only applicable to final projects/paper. The weekly tasks must be submitted as scheduled. No late submission of outputs is allowed. In case of sickness or emergencies, a certification must be secured and attached in the output. The student is expected to submit and upload an E-Portfolio in LMS containing the following
1. Critical essay and book chapter summaries - 25% 2. Group Presentations (Book Review and PESTLE Analysis) - 25% 3. Sustainability Term Paper - 30% 4. Term Paper Presentation - 20% TBA
Date: July 26, 2024
